gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: We need ___ proof before we can act (CONCLUDE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'proof': conclusive (-ive). 'Conclusion' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The trip gave us a lot of ___ (PLEASE).
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: pleasure (note the irregular spelling).

gaps.sentence: His sudden ___ came as a shock to everyone (DEPART).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject (-ure); beware the word meaning 'part of an organisation'
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'depart' is departure (-ure); a department is a section of an organisation.

gaps.sentence: She was praised for her ___ (TOLERATE) of other viewpoints.

gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.
